hero.description: Browse two core tracks, drill into curated subcategories, search papers by keyword, filter by year, and maintain your content entirely through structured JSON files.

panels.label: Track A
panels.title: AI for Economics
panels.text: AI as a research instrument for modeling, simulation, forecasting, causal analysis, and policy design.

panels.label: Track B
panels.title: Agentic Economy
panels.text: AI agents as producers, workers, market participants, and governance objects inside economic systems.

home.tracksNote: Each track expands into subcategories, reading paths, timelines, and paper cards rendered directly from JSON.
home.finderNote: Use keyword search and year filtering to locate papers quickly across all tracks.
home.featuredNote: These cards demonstrate the rendering schema. Replace or expand them by editing the JSON data files only.

trackPage.overviewNote: Open a subcategory to browse its paper list and the optional evolution timeline.
trackPage.pathNote: Designed for newcomers, literature mapping, or syllabus design.
trackPage.finderNote: Filter across all papers under the current research track.

subcategoryPage.finderNote: Search by keyword or year, then click a tag to refine quickly.
subcategoryPage.timelineNote: A concise progression from earlier modeling traditions to contemporary AI-native approaches.
subcategoryPage.papersNote: Each card supports citation text, tags, venue, year, and external links.

common.noResultsText: Try another keyword or switch back to all years.
common.emptyText: Add paper entries in the JSON files to populate this section.
common.maintainedBy: Maintained through JSON data files. No manual HTML authoring is needed for paper pages.
common.footerNote: Designed for GitHub Pages, bilingual research portals, and long-term literature curation.
